items.title: George "Pops" Foster Interview, 1957-04-21
items.q: I was working at Tranchinas at West End, with Peter Bocars and P. Ron and Arthur Campbell, Johnny Sinceria, and Tom Benton, myself.

ctx.x: Well how did you happen to go on the riverboat?
I was working at, is he ready? Yeah. I was working at Tranchinas at West End, with Peter Bocars and P. Ron and Arthur Campbell, Johnny Sinceria, and Tom Benton, myself.

items.title: Johnny St. Cyr Interview, 1958-08-27
items.q: So what he done was Pat Foster and I was in the band.

ctx.x: Do you remember anything about Jazzland, what it was like? Did you ever go there and sit in?

Well, yes. I went there and sit in with the band one night. Turpin had given a macaroni dinner for the Bullock band. And we went on out there. And the guys in the band, at least a piano player in the band, he was rated as the best blues player in St. Louis. I just remember his name. I think his name was John something. And the Russian racket just came out. It was kind of a tough number. So what he done was Pat Foster and I was in the band. Dodge was sitting in the band. And he called Indian Blues. It must have…
Oh yeah, that's a tough precaution.

items.title: George "Pops" Foster Interview, 1958-08-24
items.q: I think Jonathan says he's in May 2 or April, isn't he?

ctx.x: Yes. My mother on this side. My father is her mother. I think Jonathan says he's in May 2 or April, isn't he?
